title: Ecosystems and Biome Conservation: practice quiz

questions.text: What is ecology?
options: The study of the structure of cells
The scientific study of interactions between living organisms and their physical environment

questions.text: How many structural levels of organization does the guide list, from cell to biosphere?
Which level is a group of individuals of the same species living in a specific area at the same time?
What is a community?
options: The living and non-living parts together
All interacting populations of different species in a shared environment
A large region with a distinct climate

questions.text: An ecosystem is a community of biotic organisms interacting with...
A biome is best described as...
options: a large regional unit with distinct climate patterns, dominant vegetation, and adapted wildlife
a single group of organisms of one species
the thin layer of air around Earth

questions.text: Which level is the global sum of all ecosystems?
Which of these is an abiotic factor?
How does energy enter most ecosystems?
options: As sunlight, which producers convert into chemical energy by photosynthesis

questions.text: Which organism is a producer (Level 1)?
Primary consumers are...
options: herbivores that eat plants and algae
top predators with no natural enemies

questions.text: Which organism is a secondary consumer?
Tertiary consumers, such as the great white shark and jaguar, are...
options: apex predators with no natural enemies

questions.text: What is the role of decomposers?
options: Break down dead organic matter and recycle soil nutrients

questions.text: Deserts are defined as areas receiving less than how much annual precipitation?
About what fraction of Earth's land surface do deserts cover?
The Sahara and the Sonoran are examples of which type of desert?
The Antarctic Ice Sheet is classified as a...
Desert plants that are adapted to scarce water are called...
Which adaptation do deep-taproot desert plants use?
options: Aerial prop roots that filter salt
Vertical taproots extending 10-30 m to reach underground water

questions.text: How does the Saguaro cactus survive in the desert?
options: Its pleated stem stores a large amount of water and its leaves are reduced to spines
It has broad, dark leaves to catch sunlight
It gets water from morning dew through its feet

questions.text: Desert animals are called...
How does the dromedary camel cope with desert life?
options: Large ears that detect prey underground
Fat-storing humps, padded feet, and the ability to drink about 80 L at once

questions.text: What is the function of the fennec fox's oversized ears?
options: They channel dew to the mouth
They radiate body heat and detect underground prey

questions.text: Where does the kangaroo rat get its water?
options: It drinks from rivers each day
It produces metabolic water from dry seeds
It stores water in a hump
It absorbs rain through its skin

questions.text: How does the thorny devil collect water?
options: Grooves in its scales channel morning dew to its mouth

questions.text: Why does the sidewinder rattlesnake move sideways in a looping motion?
options: To minimize body contact with blistering hot sand

questions.text: Aquatic ecosystems cover over what part of Earth's surface?
What percentage of all water is marine (saltwater)?
The epipelagic zone extends from the surface to about...
Which ocean zone lies between 1,000 and 4,000 m?
The hadal zone is found at depths of...
Which adaptation is typical of the mesopelagic zone?
options: Bioluminescent counter-illumination and massive tubular eyes
Expanding stomachs and needle fangs only

questions.text: What do chemosynthetic bacteria at hydrothermal vents do?
options: Convert hydrogen sulfide into organic energy without sunlight

questions.text: What is the function of mangrove prop roots?
options: They filter saltwater and shield coastlines
They catch sunlight in the understory

questions.text: Tropical rainforests cover only about 6% of land but house over what share of plant and animal species?
How many vertical strata does a tropical rainforest have?
Which rainforest layer is the tallest (40-70 m)?
Emergent trees such as the kapok have flared roots called...
Epiphytes that absorb cloud moisture directly are typical of the...
Understory plants have broad, dark leaves to...
options: capture the small amount of filtered sunlight (about 2-15%)

questions.text: Which animals are typical of the rainforest understory?
options: Green iguana and poison dart frog

questions.text: Which is a primary cause of deforestation?
Overfishing by industrial trawling can trigger...
options: more sunlight in the deep sea
trophic cascades and the collapse of forage fish

questions.text: What causes oxygen-depleted 'dead zones' in water?
options: Algal blooms from agricultural fertilizer runoff (eutrophication)

questions.text: During coral bleaching, thermal stress causes corals to...
The drying of the Aral Sea is given as an example of...
What is a no-take marine reserve designed to do?
options: Restore ocean food webs by prohibiting fishing

Wildlife corridors and protected national parks help prevent...
Riparian buffer strips and wastewater treatment help to...
